input.quote: IBM assumes and will assume ownership and MSL assigns and will assign all intellectual and industrial property rights for hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered under this Agreement
input.rationale: Every licence grant in this deal runs from us (IBM) to MSL, not the other way: § 13.3(a) confirms MSL gets no rights in IBM IP beyond a royalty-free right to use disclosed confidential information solely to manufacture for IBM; § 5 of the Equipment and Program Loan Agreement licenses Loaned Programs to MSL; Attachment 6 and § 24.1 restrict MSL's use of IBM/third-party software. Those restrictions benefit us and are not flagged. In place of a licence to us, § 13.1 vests outright ownership in IBM (with assignment by MSL) of all IP in the hardware, software, design and documentation of Products delivered and of inventions made on Products and on IBM processes — a position better than the preferred licence scope, since as owner we may extend use to Related Companies and contractors, cannot have rights revoked, and may transfer to successors. MSL's only retained right is to use such inventions in performing its obligations to us. Noted but not flagged: § 24.1(a)/(b) state MSL conveys to IBM no licence in MSL or third-party software and neither party gets licence rights or source code without the owner's approval; this is mutual, sits outside the Product IP that we own, and leaves a consent path, so it is not a material licence-scope failure.
